stories.headline: Election Commission’s appeals against 16.10 lakh cleared voters raise legal questions
stories.title: Election Commission’s appeals against 16.10 lakh cleared voters raise legal questions
stories.summary: The officials who filed appeals against the inclusion of the 16.10 lakh voters may not have had the authority to do so under the Representation of the People Act; according to the Act, the CEO/DEO/ERO/AERO are the authorities with respect to electoral rolls
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A little over 16 lakh electors in West Bengal whose names had been cleared by judicial officers after being flagged for logical discrepancies during the West Bengal SIR had found themselves back in the crosshairs when the Election Commission of India (ECI) filed appeals against the inclusion of their names.
These electors would have voted in the Assembly polls in April because their names appeared on the supplementary lists published before the elections.
But the officials who filed appeals against the inclusion of the 16.10 lakh voters may not have had the authority to do so under the Representation of the People Act.
According to the Act, the CEO/DEO/ERO/AERO are the authorities with respect to electoral rolls.

In its affidavit filed before the Supreme Court on October 26, the Election Commission of India said that the appeals were not brought to its notice earlier and that a communication dated October 22, 2026, was received from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal, stating that its officials had filed the appeals in their capacity as authorities under the Act.
It further said that the “officers had the authority to file the appeals as per the orders of this Hon’ble (Supreme) Court”.

Though the ECI, in the affidavit, mentioned that the only authorities vis-à-vis electoral rolls recognised under the Act are the “CEO/DEOs/EROs/AEROs”, it did not state categorically that the appeals against inclusions were filed by these authorised officials, and mentioned them as “officers of the office of CEO West Bengal”.
The filing of appeals against voters cleared by judicial officers was one of the questions raised by Election Commissioners S. S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi in their file notings.
Opposition parties in West Bengal have called for the scrapping of these appeals and sought a judicial probe into the matter.

According to Congress leader Prasenjit Bose, one of the petitioners in the West Bengal SIR case in the top court, these “officers of the office of the CEO” who have filed appeals against inclusion in the Appellate Tribunals cannot have any authority under the Act since the Tribunals were created by the Supreme Court in April 2026 and the Act says nothing about any tribunal.
On Thursday (October 29, 2026), the Congress, in a memorandum submitted to the CEO of West Bengal, demanded that the appeals against inclusion filed by the ECI be cancelled, as they violated the Act.
It demanded an IT audit to disclose the date, time and process of filing these appeals.

stories.headline: Why is ISRO’s NVS-03 satellite launch crucial? | Explained
stories.title: Why is ISRO’s NVS-03 satellite launch crucial? | Explained
stories.summary: The mission could help restore the functioning of India’s regional satellite navigation system NavIC; its development began following the 1999 Kargil War, when the U.S reportedly clamped down on GPS data access
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The story so far: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is scheduled to launch the NVS-03 satellite on October 30, in a mission that could help restore the functioning of India’s indigenous satellite navigation system, NavIC.

The launch comes at a time when the constellation has been weakened by repeated failures of onboard atomic clocks and the inability to place its previous replacement satellite, NVS-02, in its intended orbit.

stories.headline: Bajaj, TVS, Hero post strong Q2 profit; industry sales grow 27 percent
stories.title: Bajaj, TVS, Hero post strong Q2 profit; industry sales grow 27 percent
stories.summary: The top three listed two-wheeler makers reported strong revenue growth in the September quarter as domestic demand, an export surge and fast-rising e-scooter sales outweighed a sharp rise in commodity costs. Margins and profit growth varied across the players.Bajaj Auto, the first among the three to report its results, posted its first-ever Rs 20,000 crore revenue quarter.Revenue from operations rose 34 percent to Rs 20,003 crore, and net profit rose 35 percent to Rs 3,354 crore. Ebitda climbed 37 percent to Rs 4,172 crore. The margin was 20.9 percent, up 40 basis points from a year earlier and flat from the June quarter. Total volumes rose 20 percent to 15.49 lakh units, led by exports.TVS Motor reported revenue of Rs 17,103 crore, up 44 percent, with Ebitda up 47 percent at Rs 2,219 crore. Its margin widened 30 basis points to 13.0 percent. Net profit rose 52 percent to Rs 1,377 crore. Sales reached a record 19.19 lakh units, up 27 percent.The country’s largest two-wheeler maker Hero MotoCorp had the weakest earnings growth of the three.Standalone revenue rose 21 percent to Rs 14,687 crore and Ebitda rose 8 percent to Rs 1,968 crore. Net profit grew 5 percent to Rs 1,456 crore. Its Ebitda margin was 13.4 percent, up 10 basis points from the June quarter but down about 164 bps YoY.On a consolidated basis, Hero’s profit rose 41 percent to Rs 1,861 crore, helped by a one-time Rs 397 crore gain from the equity dilution of an associate company after its capital raise.Even in terms of sales volumes, Hero had the weakest rise, with wholesale volumes up 10.5 percent to 18.68 lakh units.Explaining the reasons behind Hero’s Q2 performance, Jay Kale, Director-Institutional Equity Research at Elara Capital, said: "Hero’s EV business is just ramping up, so commodity pressures in terms of EV losses are higher for them compared to the others. For Bajaj and TVS, a better exports mix and favourable currency movement helped offset the rise in commodity costs.”Also Read: Bajaj Auto Q2 profit jumps 35 percent to Rs 3,353 crore as exports surgeIndustry DemandHero said industry retail sales rose more than 27 percent in the quarter, with internal combustion engine (ICE) models up 23 percent and electric vehicles up 82 percent.For the first half, retail rose over 20 percent, said Hero MotoCorp CEO Harshavardhan Chitale on a post-earnings call with analysts.“To understand the impact of pent-up demand of GST, we looked at growth over the two-year period [so as to strip out the impact], which was 11 percent CAGR. This shows that industry as a whole has a healthy growth momentum, even after discounting the impact of the pent-up demand,” he said.Bajaj said the industry, including electric scooters, grew 18 percent in April-August. On a post-earnings call, the management singled out motorcycles of 150cc and above and electric scooters as the main drivers.The GST cut that took effect on September 22, 2025, lowered the tax on smaller two-wheelers, and will make YoY comparisons harder in the second half.OutlookManagement at all three expect growth to slow from the pace witnessed in H1.Hero’s Chitale said he expects the industry to grow at mid-to-high single digits in the festive period and the second half. ICE models should grow at low single digits, with EVs lifting the overall number.TVS Managing Director K N Radhakrishnan, on an analyst call, said he expects “good single-digit” growth in the third quarter, citing a high base from last year.Bajaj Joint Managing Director Rakesh Sharma expects September-December growth to stay in double digits but below the April-August rate.Also Read: Ather Energy posts first profit as EV demand outstrips supplyRural DemandThe monsoon this year is the weakest in over a decade, with a 13 percent deficit in rainfall. Parts of India are also facing droughts.Hero said rural performance matched or beat urban in the quarter and so far in the festive period. Fears of a weak monsoon have not fully played out, with sowing close to last year’s level, it said.TVS said EV growth in rural markets was slightly higher than in urban markets in the first half.Bajaj was more cautious. Sharma said that drought-like conditions in Maharashtra, parts of the south and the northeast could hurt more in the fourth quarter. He said growth is skewed toward higher-income buyers, with entry-level products lagging, a “K-shaped” pattern that may get sharper.Input CostsBajaj said commodity and other input inflation was about 3-3.5 percent of revenue in the quarter, on top of about 4.5 percent in the first.The magnitude of this cost escalation is ‘unprecedented’, creating significant pressure on the business with inflation of a scale that we would typically see spread over many years, the management said.Price increases covered 50-60 percent of the impact in the first half. The balance was largely offset through favourable currency realisation and continued cost optimisation initiatives, it said.TVS said material costs rose about 1.9 percent from the June quarter, against price hikes of 1.6 percent. It has taken small increases in October and will review pricing after Diwali.Hero said commodity inflation was about 1 percent sequentially, and about half of the roughly 5.5 percent cumulative inflation in the first half has been passed on.It said margins should be stable in the third quarter and that Hero remains on track toward its 14-16 percent medium-term target.ExportsBajaj’s exports rose 41 percent to 7.79 lakh units, with shipments to Africa nearly doubling. Management said it aims to sustain about 7.5 lakh units a quarter. TVS reported record international sales of 5.39 lakh units, up 35 percent.Hero was the outlier. Its overseas dispatches fell about 24 percent to 85,000 units, hurt by port and customs disruption after an earthquake in a key Latin American market and weaker demand in Bangladesh after a fuel-price spike linked to the Gulf conflict. Colombia accounts for close to a quarter of Hero’s exports. Retail sales abroad still rose 19 percent, and Hero expects double-digit dispatch growth to return in the third and fourth quarters.Electric VehiclesEVs were the fastest-growing segment at all three companies. Bajaj’s electric two- and three-wheelers reached a record 2 lakh units, now a third of domestic revenue.Its Chetak scooter had its biggest quarter, with revenue above Rs 2,000 crore and a market share of about 23 percent. Bajaj said the EV business is now accretive to domestic margins but still dilutive for the company as a whole. Chetak capacity will rise to 80,000 a month by the fourth quarter.TVS sold 1.86 lakh electric two-wheelers, up 133 percent. Hero’s Vida retailed about 66,000 units, up 74 percent. Vida turned gross-margin positive, with its EBITDA drag narrowing to Rs 168 crore from Rs 232 crore in the June quarter.Hero’s EV market share was 11.1 percent in the quarter and about 13.5-14 percent in October so far. Hero plans to lift Vida capacity to 45,000 a month by the fourth quarter. Production-linked incentives helped all three, and Bajaj said it has reached the top PLI rate of 18 percent for the second half.PremiumisationBajaj is repositioning around motorcycles of 125cc and above. It chose to raise prices on 100cc models ahead of rivals and accepted weaker volumes there. Domestic two-wheeler volumes rose just 2 percent to 6.07 lakh units. It said refreshed Pulsars made up 33 percent of its 125cc-plus sales in the festive period so far. KTM and Triumph sold about 40,000 units, up 31 percent.Hero launched the Xtreme 160R and 250R in October and plans three to four more premium launches this financial year. It has 150 Premia stores. Premium market share was still just 1.9 percent in the first half. TVS is expanding Norton, though management conceded subsidiary losses are elevated. Scooters and EVs also lifted average realisations at all three companies.

stories.title: Supreme Court verdict clears way for Miyapur land takeover
stories.summary: Following the Supreme Court's landmark ruling on Miyapur lands, Rangareddy District Collector inspects 550 acres of government land, confirming 400 acres fenced.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: Following the Supreme Court's landmark ruling on Miyapur lands, Rangareddy District Collector inspects 550 acres of government land, confirming 400 acres fenced.

Hyderabad: Following the Supreme Court’s verdict, the officials have swiftly started the process of acquiring about 550 acres of government land under Miyapur survey numbers 100 and 101 in Serilingampalli revenue mandal of Rangareddy district as the district collector C Narayan Reddy said that about 400 acres of land is already fenced.
The Collector informed that the government will not touch the residential colonies which have come up in the area after consultation with the government.
The Rangareddy district collector Narayana Reddy inspected these lands worth thousands of crores of rupees on Friday, along with officials of revenue and HMDA.
The collector said that 400 acres were already fenced and the remaining land needs to be fenced.

He said that this was the long legal dispute that has been going on for almost 30 years since the 1995 Land Grabbing Case (LGC) has been permanently ended with a historic verdict by the Supreme Court.
As the Supreme Court has made it clear that the land belongs to the government, the land inspection and acquisition supervision was undertaken under the by the district collector.
The collector said that the Supreme Court has given a land mark judgement in the survey no 100 and 101.
“As per the court orders we will implement.
We thank Justice Satish Chandra Sharma and MN Sundereshan for this judgement for the peope of the state.
This is the case, which was in the court for 23 long years through Civil appeal 10699 of 2013.
As per the judgement, the 550 acres land belongs government.

stories.headline: Supreme Court seeks report from ECI on Form 7 misuse allegations
stories.title: Supreme Court seeks report from ECI on Form 7 misuse allegations
stories.summary: Election Commission says it did not accept any Form 7s filed in violation of norms in U.P.; poll officials took prompt corrective steps, it says after Congress MP alleges widespread fraud during SIR
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Election Commission of India (EC) told the Supreme Court on Friday (October 30, 2026) that though it found “false” Form 7s for deletion of voters during the Uttar Pradesh Special Intensive Revision (SIR), none of them were accepted.

Appearing before a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, senior advocate Dama Seshadri Naidu, for the ECI, said corrective measures were taken promptly on discovery of such “false” forms.
Authorities had rejected Form 7s filed in violation of norms, the ECI said.

The ECI was responding to allegations levelled in a petition filed by Congress’ Barabanki MP Tanuj Punia, represented by senior advocate Salman Khurshid and advocate Shariq Ahmed, about widespread misuse and fraud in connection with bulk filing of Form 7 during the claims-and-objections phase of the Uttar Pradesh SIR.
Mr. Ahmed questioned the ECI’s claim that false Form 7s were stopped at the gates.
He said the court must subject this claim to judicial scrutiny.
Counsel argued that it was exactly the lack of any corrective measures in the Uttar Pradesh SIR that “emboldened” the filing of bulk Form 7s in Karnataka and Telangana.
“Of the 32 Form 7s in the Hata Assembly constituency in Uttar Pradesh, two were signed by the booth-level officer.
All these forms pertained to deletion of voters belonging to one community,” counsel submitted.
The court asked Mr. Ahmed to submit a note with details and additional information, if any, on the issue.
“Let the ECI look into these issues, take necessary action and file a compliance report,” the court observed.
The Uttar Pradesh SIR process ended in April with the final voter list showing a reported 84 lakh increase in the electorate to 13.39 crore.

stories.headline: Rising power bills spark resentment across Kashmir
stories.title: Rising power bills spark resentment across Kashmir
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 29: Consumers across several parts of Kashmir have expressed resentment over the recent electricity tariff hike, alleging that rising bills and irregular power supply have added to the financial burden on ordinary households. After an elected government returned to power in Jammu and Kashmir, many residents had hoped for relief from rising living costs. However, consumers say the reported six percent increase in electricity tariffs, along with alleged hikes exceeding nine percent in some non-metered areas, has left them disappointed. Consumers have questioned the gap between the government's promises of relief, including the proposed benefit of 200 units of free electricity for eligible households, and the bills they claim to be receiving. Advocate G. N. Bukhari, who practices at the Additional District & Sessions Court, Handwara, raised concerns over electricity bills issued to consumers in North Kashmir. He alleged that some households had received bills showing increases beyond the approved six percent hike, with certain consumers claiming that their bills had nearly doubled. "Consumers from North Kashmir have every right to know why their electricity bills are increasing beyond the announced tariff revision. The authorities must explain the basis of these charges and ensure that no household is overbilled," Bukhari said. Local residents said the situation was particularly difficult for families dependent on daily wages, who are already struggling to manage household expenses amid rising prices. Shamim Ahmad, a resident of Langate and a daily-wage laborer of the Jal Shakti Department, said his electricity bill had increased from Rs 1,300 in the previous month to Rs 1,420 for September. "I earn my livelihood through daily labor. Some days I find work, while on other days I return home empty-handed. My electricity bill has increased despite our limited income. It becomes difficult to manage household expenses when every essential service keeps getting costlier," he said. Ahmad questioned the increase in his bill and urged the authorities to verify the charges. "People like us cannot afford unexpected increases in monthly bills. If the approved hike is six percent, the authorities should explain why consumers are being charged more," he added. Residents have demanded transparency in tariff calculations and sought an explanation from the Kashmir Power Distribution Corporation Limited (KPDCL) regarding the complaints. They urged the government and the Power Development Department to investigate allegations of inflated billing, verify meter readings, review tariff calculations, and ensure that consumers are charged strictly according to approved rates. However, none of the officials from KPDCL were available to comment on this issue.

Shamim Ahmad, a resident of Langate and a daily-wage laborer of the Jal Shakti Department, said his electricity bill had increased from Rs 1,300 in the previous month to Rs 1,420 for September.
"I earn my livelihood through daily labor.
Some days I find work, while on other days I return home empty-handed.
My electricity bill has increased despite our limited income.
It becomes difficult to manage household expenses when every essential service keeps getting costlier," he said.
Ahmad questioned the increase in his bill and urged the authorities to verify the charges.
"People like us cannot afford unexpected increases in monthly bills.
If the approved hike is six percent, the authorities should explain why consumers are being charged more," he added.
Residents have demanded transparency in tariff calculations and sought an explanation from the Kashmir Power Distribution Corporation Limited (KPDCL) regarding the complaints.

They urged the government and the Power Development Department to investigate allegations of inflated billing, verify meter readings, review tariff calculations, and ensure that consumers are charged strictly according to approved rates.
However, none of the officials from KPDCL were available to comment on this issue.

stories.headline: J&K Cabinet approves two new industrial estates
stories.title: J&K Cabinet approves two new industrial estates
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 30: The Council of Ministers, recently chaired by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, has approved the establishment of two new Industrial Estates in Jammu & Kashmir, involving a combined investment of Rs 162.72 crore. The approved projects include a New Industrial Estate at Pehlipora, Lar, Ganderbal, at a cost of Rs 60.92 crore, and Industrial Estate Bhagthali (Part-II), Kathua, at a cost of Rs 101.80 crore. The Chief Minister said the projects would strengthen industrial infrastructure, attract investment, promote local manufacturing and create new employment opportunities for the youth. He added that these initiatives would contribute to sustained economic growth and further strengthen the industrial ecosystem across Jammu & Kashmir.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks Centre to take measures against online misuse of court feeds
stories.title: Supreme Court asks Centre to take measures against online misuse of court feeds
stories.summary: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta submits that suggestions from various High Courts and other stakeholders have been received and forwarded to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (October 30, 2026) asked the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to formulate measures against the commercial exploitation of live-streamed judicial proceedings in violation of earlier court orders.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant recorded Solicitor General Tushar Mehta’s submission that suggestions from various High Courts and other stakeholders had already been received and forwarded to the Ministry.
Mr. Mehta submitted that the Ministry would consider the suggestions and respond in a few days.
He sought listing of the plea for further consideration after the Deepavali vacation.
He also flagged violations of earlier orders and urged the court to consider directing the removal of material uploaded in breach of its restrictions.

The court had recently passed orders banning the unauthorised use and circulation of live-streamed judicial proceedings on social media and digital platforms, saying that anything meant for the public good cannot be exploited commercially for personal gain.
“Necessary measures for taking action against those who fail to comply with the directions will also be incorporated in the policy regime,” the court observed.

Advocate Prashant Bhushan suggested that every official clip released by the court should carry a verifiable digital signature or watermark, enabling the public and digital platforms to distinguish genuine footage from manipulated versions.
He further suggested that all court proceedings should be made available on the Supreme Court’s website in an authenticated and watermarked format.

The court is examining the issue amid concerns over the unauthorised extraction, modification, circulation, and commercial use of video clips of judicial proceedings, often accompanied by misleading captions or representations.
